parsed.rationale: Both `AsyncNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/AsyncMessage.swift:39) and `MainActorNotificationMessage` (Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/MainActorMessage.swift:43) are interfaces in the same `Core` package that share two identical members — `makeNotification:(_ message: Self, object: Subject?) -> Notification` and `name:Notification.Name` — differing only in the concurrency annotation on `makeMessage` (`sending Notification` vs plain `Notification`). Extracting the shared members into a common parent protocol (e.g., `NotificationMessage`) within the same `Core` package eliminates the duplication while allowing each child to retain its distinct `makeMessage` signature reflecting its concurrency contract. No restraint markers are present on either record, making this a clean refactor opportunity. The alternative of a default-implementation extension is weaker here because the differing `makeMessage` signatures mean the protocols genuinely diverge in their primary factory method, making inheritance the more expressive model.
